sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Cinda-Regi-Tiyal language [cdr] (as of 2025-11-03)
sources.note: Inventory only: SIL 2007 survey wordlists, Dancy 1966 Swadesh list, PARADISEC RB5 Cinda/Turegi/Kamuku wordlists, literacy booklets, Mort 2012 phonology (not online), Mort 2021 dictionary, Dettweiler 2003, Spencer et al. 2014. The only 'language description' is Mort 2012.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. In Peter K. Austin & Stuart McGill (eds.), Language Documentation and Description 11, 90-135. London: SOAS.
sources.note: Open-access overview of the northwest Kainji languages including Kamuku with typological notes; low chance of a stress remark but unverified (lddjournal.org could not be reached by automated download, IA offline).

sources.citation: Mort, Katharine (comp.). 2021. Kamuku Dictionary (Kamuku-Hausa-English), self-reviewed draft, 465 entries. SIL International / Webonary (site pages Phonology, Grammar, Introduction, Alphabet; downloaded via r.jina.ai reader proxy).
sources.note: Nothing: the 'Phonology' and 'Grammar' pages are empty Webonary placeholders; Introduction (250 Cinda nouns with Regi/Kuki equivalents) and Alphabet (24 letters) say nothing about tone or stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (entry 74 'Cinda-Regi-Rogo-Kuki cluster'; bibliography p.148).
sources.note: Nothing; entry lists 'Refs: Phonology: Mort (2012)' and the bibliography gives 'Mort, Katherine 2012. A Phonological Description of the Cinda dialect of the Kamuku language. ms.'

sources.citation: Spencer, Katharine; Magnusson, Carol; Yoder, Zach; Hannelová, Katarína; Otronyi, Linus; Oro, Yakubu; Rueck, Michael J. 2014. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the 'Yara (Kamuku) people, Niger and Kaduna States, Nigeria. SIL International, vi+77 pp. (SIL archive 60335)
sources.note: Open PDF by the same author (Spencer = Mort) covering Cinda/Regi/Kuki/Kuru/Maruba; may carry wordlist transcription conventions or a phonology note;org not reachable by automated download, Internet Archive offline).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 369 pp. (sec. 4.5.1 'Cinda', pp. 32-34 = pp. 39-41)
sources.note: Nothing: 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in 369 pp. Cinda phonology (adapted from Mort n.d.): consonants, 6 vowels, nasality; p.33 'The tone inventory of Cinda is analysed as two level tones.. Cinda makes use of both lexical and grammatical tone'; tone lexicalised as a morpheme melody (preserved in reversed speech); automatic/non-automatic downstep p.34.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. 'Kamuku languages' web page, rogerblench.info Kainji/Kamuku/KmkOP.htm (Internet Archive copy 2015-04-20); = the 'Blench (ms) The Kamuku languages' named by the earlier scan
sources.note: Nothing; classification blurb and tree only. the Internet Archive's index listing shows the Kamuku folder never held a PDF or wordlist.

sources.note: The only phonological description of the language; its table of contents has a dedicated chapter '9 Stress' (after '8 Tone') plus syllable/root/word structure chapters -- almost certainly contains the deciding statement. Cited as the phonology source by Blench & McGill 2012 and Blench's Atlas 2020.

sources.note: Title/record only. A grammar draft by the author of the only phonological description in the cluster will almost certainly restate the Cinda tone analysis (Blench & McGill 2012 sec. 4.5.1, after Mort: two level tones H and L with downstep) and may add grammatical-tone facts; it says nothing first-hand about Rogo.
